model_interpretation.claim: Un mapping multi-lignes par CTA peut réduire le nombre de CTA pour les réductions étroites, tandis que le mapping T1 à une ligne par CTA conserve son option pour les lignes larges. Le dispatch utilise des bandes de largeur rembourrée génériques; le bénéfice de l’hybride reste à mesurer.

model_interpretation.claim: Test one warp for every one-row CTA. This may reduce coordination overhead, but increases per-thread work, especially for wide rows. The selected two-warp parent measured 41.616 µs; the best observed 4-warps-below-4096/2-warps-otherwise candidate measured 41.243 µs, so this configuration is only an improvement if it passes correctness and beats that measured result.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.py"],"retained":["Retain one program/CTA per complete row and the stable masked max-exp-sum-normalize computation.","Use one warp for each row as a bounded launch-configuration contrast; do not introduce multi-row CTAs or streaming loops.","Preserve existing tail masks, stride handling, dtype behavior, output layout, and fallback path."]}

model_interpretation.claim: Earlier grouped candidates were correct but clustered between 42.549 and 42.640 µs, so they do not establish a grouping benefit. This trial increases rows per CTA for padded widths through 256 while keeping the row-column tile no larger than 4096 elements through width 1024. Fewer CTAs may help narrow rows, but increased per-CTA state may hurt occupancy. Compare the measured result with T1's 42.154 µs target and official candidates; no speedup is assumed.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.py"],"retained":["Increase rows per CTA to 32, 16, 8, and 4 for padded widths up to 128, 256, 512, and 1024 respectively; retain 2 rows for wider widths.","Keep the existing 4-warps-through-1024 and 8-warps-for-wider configuration and the complete-row, masked, max-subtracted per-row reductions.","Preserve the existing stride-aware accesses, output allocation, and empty-dimension handling."]}

model_interpretation.claim: The best measured streaming variant averaged 56.096 µs using 4 warps and 1024-element tiles for widths up to 1024, otherwise 2048-element tiles. This experiment retains that tile policy but uses 8 warps only for wider rows. More warps may reduce per-thread tile work, though scheduling and reduction overhead could outweigh that benefit. The candidate awaits official correctness and timing; compare its result to the measured 4-warp variant.

items.objective: Implement the direct, non-streaming Triton design with one program/CTA owning one complete row: masked load, stable max/exp/sum, and normalized store. Compare with the official tutorial and explore configurations for this one-row mapping only. Do not switch to multi-row CTAs or streaming loops. Support arbitrary valid widths and tails, preserve the stated accuracy and input/output requirements, and retain only correctness-passing measured improvements.

items.subject: Streaming online reduction to reduce live row state
items.objective: Explore a single-CTA-per-row streaming softmax that processes column tiles while maintaining a numerically stable running maximum and rescaled sum, then rereads tiles to produce normalized output. This tests whether reducing live per-row state outweighs extra input traffic for the performance shape. Support arbitrary widths and tails, preserve the stated accuracy and input/output requirements, and retain the approach only if official measurements justify it.

items.subject: Intégration mesurée des mappings direct et groupé
items.objective: À partir du meilleur candidat T1, intégrer le noyau T2 à plusieurs lignes par CTA comme alternative sélectionnée selon des dimensions génériques, sans seuil calé sur les seules formes de test. Mesurer le programme intégré selon le protocole officiel.
